title: Metric Deprecation Play & Trace Bridge — Notes
content:
Context and purpose:

This note captures a repeatable playbook for safely deprecating metrics and making sure traces remain useful after metric removal. We want to reduce metric sprawl, improve dashboard clarity, and avoid losing diagnostic signal for oncall and runbook flows. This is a living working doc — not an endpoint.

Why a 'trace bridge'?
- When a metric is removed, historic dashboards and runbooks that referenced it break. Traces carry high-cardinality context and event boundaries; by mapping traces to the retiring metric (and enriching traces before removal) we retain the investigatory path.
- The bridge is an operational pattern: augment traces (and span tags) to replicate the metric's signal or to point to replacement metrics before the metric is turned off.

Scope:
- Applies to any counter/gauge/histogram owned by runtime and platform teams (serving-runtime, edge-routing, batching, kv-cache).
- Excludes ephemeral debug-only metrics (those gated behind debug flags and never on dashboards).

Owners and approvals:
- Metric owner: team owning the instrumentation (e.g., serving-runtime/kv-cache).
- Observability steward: Elena Rivera (eng-observability) — coordinates deprecation window and validates replacement coverage.
- Oncall lead sign-off required for production-facing metrics.
- Product/SE stakeholders notified for customer-exposed dashboards.

High-level steps (play):
1) Inventory & rationale
  - Add metric to the 'deprecation candidate' list in Confluence with owner, query, dashboards referencing it, and sample alert rules (copy exact PromQL/SQL).
  - Provide a short rationale (why deprecated: replaced, noisy, wrong cardinality, cost).
2) Trace mapping and enrichment plan (trace bridge)
  - Identify span(s) that represent the logical operation the metric measured (e.g., token-gen.start, kv-cache.hit, route.dispatch).
  - Define an enrichment patch: add a stable span tag like telemetry.metric_bridge=<metric_name> and telemetry.metric_value_hint=<low|medium|high> or telemetry.metric_value_numeric when feasible.
  - If metric was a histogram, capture boundaries distribution as span tags (bucket_low/bucket_high) or attach a short proto payload on the root span for offline analysis. Keep tags small and boolean where possible.
3) Dashboard & alert migration
  - Create replacement panels that use new metrics or trace-derived aggregates. Add them next to existing panels (side-by-side) for the audit window.
  - Update runbook entries with 'if old metric missing, use X trace-derived query' and include example trace links.
4) Canary / audit window
  - Enable enrichment in a small subset of servers (10% traffic) for 48–72 hours. Run sampling on traces to ensure tags are present and indexable.
  - Observability steward inspects dashboards for parity and oncall runs simulated incidents using traces.
5) Sunset and rollback plan
  - After 2–4 week audit and no regressions, schedule metric disable. Keep enrichment code for an additional 2 weeks to allow historical alignment.
  - If significant loss of diagnostic capability is detected, rollback by reintroducing metric and re-evaluating replacement approach.

Instrumentation checklist before removal:
- [ ] Add telemetry.metric_bridge tag to root span (string with metric logical name).
- [ ] If metric numeric is small-cost, include telemetry.metric_value_numeric (int/float).
- [ ] Ensure sampling rate of traces that include the new tag is >= 1% across all services and >= 5% for critical services for the audit window.
- [ ] Add example trace ids to Confluence for test incidents.
- [ ] Update metric inventory and add deprecation timeline.

PromQL examples (copy/paste friendly) — use only for reference in dashboards and migration PRs:
- Original metric: sum(rate(inference_token_emit_total[1m])) by (model, region)
- Replacement (trace-derived synthetic counter approximation via trace logs): sum by (model, region) (increase(trace_metric_bridge_total{telemetry_metric_bridge="inference_token_emit_total"}[5m]))
- Trace-fallback panel (count of traces with bridge tag): sum(rate(jaeger_spans_total{telemetry_metric_bridge="inference_token_emit_total"}[5m]))

Dashboard migration UX notes:
- When placing the replacement next to original, add a small annotation on the panel title: "shadow: trace-bridge" and a tooltip describing how to interpret differences.
- Color-code retired-metric panels in gray and add an overlay 'DEPRECATED' tag for 30 days.
- Provide a single 'migration checklist' widget for each dashboard grouping that shows status: enrichment deployed, sampling ok, replacement visible, alerts migrated.

Alerting considerations:
- Do not change alert thresholds during audit window. Instead create duplicate alerts pointing at replacement metric and mark them 'testing' (no paging). This preserves SLO behavior while validating signal.
- If replacement is trace-derived and higher variance expected, consider increasing evaluation window or using p99 over 5m instead of instantaneous.

Trace storage and cost guardrails:
- Avoid placing high-cardinality free-form strings on spans. Prefer enumerated keys (e.g., metric_bridge: 1,2,3 mapped in Confluence) or short hashed IDs.
- If full numeric payloads are necessary, only attach them when sample_rate trace==1 in canary; otherwise compute and attach compact aggregates.

Communication plan:
- Pre-notice (1 week): Send note to #observability, owners, and affected product channels: deprecation rationale, replacement path, audit window.
- Mid-canary (end of week 1): Short summary of initial findings and dashboards showing side-by-side variability.
- Pre-sunset (2–3 weeks): Reminder and exact disable time.
- Post-sunset: Archive panels and remove metric from active inventory. Keep an audit record of the change (who/when/why).

Small runbook: "How to investigate after metric is removed" (short):
1) If an alert fires still referencing old metric, check if alert disabled — if disabled, find the migrated alert.
2) Open a trace sample for the time window (use dashboard link: 'open traces' next to panel).
3) Inspect root span tags for telemetry.metric_bridge and telemetry.metric_value_*. If present, use trace filters by service/model/region to approximate the metric trend.
4) If not present, escalate to metric owner and observability steward and consider immediate rollback.

Edge cases and gotchas:
- Metrics emitted client-side (SDKs in customers) cannot be enriched server traces; plan a different migration (SDK update with mapping telemetry).
- Metrics used solely in long-term billing reports must be kept or exported before removal.
- Some dashboards combine multiple deprecated metrics; migration must consider composite panels and aggregate equivalence.

Appendix A — Short mapping examples:
- metric: kv_cache_hit_total
  span: kv-cache.op
  tag: telemetry_metric_bridge="kv_cache_hit_total"
  numeric_hint: telemetry_metric_value_numeric = 1 (for hit) or 0 (for miss)

- metric: batching_request_ms_bucket (histogram)
  span: batch.collect
  tags: telemetry_metric_bridge="batching_request_ms_bucket", telemetry_bucket_low="0", telemetry_bucket_high="50"

Appendix B — Suggested PR checklist for deprecation change:
- Link to Confluence inventory entry and this doc.
- Attach sample traces and proof-of-enrichment.
- Add dashboard screenshot with side-by-side panels.
- Add testing plan and rollback instructions.
- Add a line item to the release notes and weekly digest.

Open questions (to resolve):
- What retention period do we have for span tag lookups? If trace retention < metric archive, we need to export enriched trace metadata to a long-term store. (Action: SRE to confirm retention policy, OBS-3421).
- Can we standardize an internal enum for telemetry.metric_bridge values to avoid free-form strings? (Action: telemetry API design ticket).

Next steps (this week):
- Owner teams to submit 'candidate list' entries for Q1 cleanup cycle.
- Observability steward to schedule a migration backlog grooming session (invite: observability, serving-runtime, platform-eng).
- Create a template PR in the telemetry repo that performs the enrichment change (branch: metric-deprecation-template).

---
NOTE: Keep this doc lightweight and copyable into PR descriptions and Confluence entries. The aim is to make deprecation low-friction while retaining the ability to investigate incidents after metrics are removed.
